issue.title: [python3] 'show arp' and 'show ndp' not work after updated to python3

failure.body:
**Description**
Commands ```show arp``` and ```show ndp``` print nothing after updated to python3.
The root cause is that ```nbrshow``` called by ```show arp``` and ```show ndp``` have an issue in handling the output of ```arp -n```.
In python3, the type of output is ```bytes``` rather than ```str```. So the match of str will fail.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Run ```show arp``` or ```show ndp```
2.
3.

**Describe the results you received:**
The IP address and MAC of neighbors will show up.

**Describe the results you expected:**
Nothing is printed.

resolution.title: [nbrshow] Convert the output of 'arp -n' from bytes to str.
resolution.description:
Signed-off-by: bingwang <<EMAIL>>

**- What I did**
Fix https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/6085

The output of 'arp -n' is bytes in python3, as a result, the search of 'ether' or other str failed. This commit addresses the issue.

I guess there are similar issues when upgrading to python3. I think we need to come up with a universal method to address these issues.

**- How I did it**
Convert the output of 'arp -n' from bytes to str.

**- How to verify it**
Verified on dx010-6, running master image.
```
admin@str2-dx010-acs-6:~$ show arp
Address       MacAddress         Iface            Vlan
------------  -----------------  ---------------  ------
<IP>      <IPV6>  PortChannel0002  -
<IP>      <IPV6>  PortChannel0005  -
......
<IP>   <IPV6>  eth0             -
<IP>  <IPV6>  eth0             -
Total number of entries 26
```
```
admin@str2-dx010-acs-6:~$ show ndp
Address                    MacAddress         Iface            Vlan    Status
-------------------------  -----------------  ---------------  ------  ---------
fc00::1a                   <IPV6>  PortChannel0011  -       REACHABLE
fc00::2                    <IPV6>  PortChannel0002  -       REACHABLE
......
fe80::<IPV6>  <IPV6>  PortChannel0005  -       STALE
fe80::<IPV6>   <IPV6>  eth0             -       STALE
```
